literal.step: README.md:L46 python setup.py install
literal.why: The README's source-install command python setup.py install imports setuptools, which a plain Python 3.12 venv no longer ships, and the README adds no step to install it (the PyPI line at L23 would work, but the source path as written fails).

literal.step: README.md:L54-L88 Simple Example (imports matplotlib) after install at L24
literal.why: The README's example imports matplotlib.pyplot but its install line gluonts[torch] does not install matplotlib and no README line adds it.

literal.step: README.md:L91 Install Python 3.7.0 then README.md:L92 pip install -r requirements.txt
literal.why: The README requires Python 3.7.0 (not installable on Ubuntu 24.04, uv has no 3.7) and its requirements.txt contradicts it: torch>=2.6.0 needs Python 3.9+ while numpy==1.15.4 and scipy==1.1.0 need 3.7 or older, so no single Python satisfies the README.

literal.step: docs/build-debug.md:L6 pnpm run install:all (README.md:L17 points to the build docs)
literal.why: docs/build-debug.md tells the reader to install nodejs 16.x and then run pnpm, but never says to install pnpm, and nodejs 16 does not ship it.

literal.step: README.md:L70 finalized_model = quantizer.finalize() (Usage snippet, after README.md:L16 pip install coreai-opt)
literal.why: The README's own Usage snippet calls quantizer.finalize(), which needs the coreai-torch package, but the install step (pip install coreai-opt) does not pull it in and the README only lists coreai-torch under 'Related projects'.

literal.step: docs/installation_guide.md:L32 pip install parl gym (Python 3.10, inside the guide's 3.7 - 3.10 range)
literal.why: The guide allows Python 3.7 - 3.10; on 3.10, pip install parl pulls its pinned grpcio==1.37.0, which has no 3.10 wheel, and building it from source fails (No module named 'pkg_resources').

literal.step: docs/vibevoice-realtime-0.5b.md:L100 pip install -e .[streamingtts] then L120 demo
literal.why: The documented pip install leaves torch unpinned (got 2.15.0) and the demo's weights_only=True load of the bundled voice preset fails with it; only the GPU docker image (older torch) is verified, and that is the step we skipped as GPU-only.

literal.step: README.md:L630 paddlex --pipeline OCR (CPU build from README.md:L596)
literal.why: The README's CPU install (paddlepaddle==3.3.0, L596) and its own OCR command with --device cpu (L625) crash inside Paddle's oneDNN backend.
literal.short: OCR crashes on README's CPU build

literal.step: README.md:L38 pip install kats
literal.why: pip install kats 0.2.0 pins numpy<1.22 (1.21.x), which has no Python 3.12 wheel and its sdist needs distutils, so the README's one install command fails on any current Python and the README names no supported Python version.

literal.step: INSTALL.md:L23 conda install pytorch=1.13.0 torchvision pytorch-cuda=11.6 -c pytorch -c nvidia, then L129 pip install -e .
literal.why: The README's pinned pytorch 1.13.0 gets an mkl 2025 from conda-forge, and importing torch then fails, so the install's own setup.py cannot run.

literal.step: docs/getting-started/prerequisites.md:L93 local/install_deps.bash
literal.why: The prerequisites page installs Python 3.11 and then runs local/install_deps.bash, which calls python3.11 -m pipenv; no step in the docs installs pipenv (the page also lists Ubuntu up to 20.04 as supported).

literal.step: INSTALL.md:L20 python -m pip install -e detectron2
literal.why: INSTALL.md:L20 builds in pip's isolated build env, where setup.py imports torch, so it fails right after the README's own torch install (no --no-build-isolation mentioned).

literal.step: docs/en/inference_deployment/whl_deploy_en.md:L37 pip install -v -e .
literal.why: The repo's requirements.txt pins numpy==1.24.4 (no Python 3.12 wheel), so pip builds it from source with setuptools 59.2.0 and crashes; the README states no Python version and its install pages (README_en.md:L54-L55) are dead links.

literal.step: README.md:L251 pip install modelscope[nlp] -f ...
literal.why: The README's nlp install pulls an unpinned transformers 5.23.0 that removed a function modelscope 1.40.3 imports, so the NLP pipeline cannot import.

literal.step: README.md:L171 python funclip/videoclipper.py --stage 2 --file ... --dest_text ...
literal.why: The README's CLI stage 2 command crashes in video_clip() (videoclipper.py:344) because the CLI path never sets self.lang, whatever dest_text is given.

literal.step: README.md:L182 pip install evalscope, then README.md:L206-209 Method 2 evalscope eval --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
literal.why: The README's Method 2 local-model command needs torch, but its only install step (pip install evalscope) does not install torch and the README does not mention it.

literal.step: oracle t.py line 32: verifier(...).verify_and_decode_transaction(tx)
literal.why: README.md:L18 installs the PyPI release (3.1.2) whose method is verify_and_decode_signed_transaction; the test calls a method name that exists only in the repo source, which the README never mentions or tells you to install.

literal.step: oracle script: import numpy as np, torch, torch.nn as nn; import coremltools as ct (torch conversion + sklearn)
literal.why: README.md:35 only says pip install coremltools and gives no demo; the test converts a PyTorch model and a scikit-learn model, which the README never asks for.

literal.step: README.md:L27 pip install gemma (after L22 pip install jax); setup.log has no pip output
literal.why: setup.log holds only the timeout line (no pip output was captured), the script is just the two README installs, and a pip dry-run of jax+gemma resolves in about 24 s here, so the 90-minute hang is most likely a stalled or very slow download/resolve of gemma's huge dependency tree (kauldron, tensorflow, xmanager, google-cloud-aiplatform) in the harness, not a README error; exact stage cannot be proven from the log.

literal.step: README.md:L182 ollama pull gpt-oss:20b
literal.why: The README's Ollama path works on a normal Linux machine, where the installer starts the server through systemd; a container has no systemd, and a 20B model is beyond a CPU runner anyway.
